name: Sogan Dolma (Turkish Stuffed Onion)
reasons: Technique baked -> simmered; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Peel onions. Boil whole in water for 10–12 minutes until outer layers soften.
Cool and carefully separate the outer layers to use as wraps. Reserve inner parts, chop and sauté.
Mix sautéed onion with rice, pine nuts, currants, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and a little oil.
Place filling inside each onion layer and roll up. Pack tightly in a pot.
Mix tomato paste with water and lemon juice. Pour over dolma.
Simmer covered for 35–40 minutes until rice is cooked. Serve at room temperature.

name: Spatzle with Butter
reasons: Technique baked -> boiled; follow the stored preparation steps. Cold assembled dishes use the existing raw category, which does not imply all ingredients are uncooked.

steps.display_text: Mix flour, eggs, milk, nutmeg, and salt into a thick, sticky batter. Beat until it pulls into strings.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Press batter through a spätzle press or colander with large holes directly into boiling water.
Boil until they float, then 1 more minute. Remove with a slotted spoon.
In a pan, heat butter until it foams and turns golden brown. Toss spätzle in the browned butter.
Season with salt and scatter fresh chives. Serve as a side or main.

name: Spinach and Feta Börek
reasons: Normalize the time tier and quick-meal tag to strict under-30 / under-45 / under-60 boundaries.

steps.display_text: Thaw and squeeze out all moisture from spinach. Mix with crumbled feta, dill, and a beaten egg.
Cut filo into strips about 8 cm wide. Brush with olive oil.
Place a spoonful of filling at one end of a filo strip. Fold into a triangle, flipping over and over to the end.
Brush triangles with oil.
Either bake at 190°C for 20–25 minutes until golden, or pan-fry in shallow oil for 2–3 minutes per side.

name: Spring Rolls
reasons: Technique fried -> raw; follow the stored preparation steps. Cold assembled dishes use the existing raw category, which does not imply all ingredients are uncooked.

steps.display_text: Cook rice vermicelli according to package. Rinse in cold water and drain.
Julienne carrot and cucumber. Slice avocado.
Fill a large bowl with warm water. Dip one rice paper wrapper for 10–15 seconds until pliable.
Lay wrapper on a damp surface. Place herbs first, then noodles and vegetables on the lower third.
Fold the bottom up, fold sides in, and roll tightly forward.
Serve with a dipping sauce made from hoisin sauce, peanut butter, lime juice, and water.

name: Strukli (Croatian Cheese Pastry)
reasons: Technique fried -> baked; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
Estimate 30 min active dough/filling/shaping; include 30 min dough rest, 10 min boiling and 20 min baking.

steps.display_text: Make soft dough from flour, egg, oil, and warm water. Knead until smooth. Rest 30 minutes.
Mix cottage cheese with eggs, sour cream, and salt for the filling.
Roll dough very thin on a floured cloth. Spread filling evenly over the dough.
Using the cloth, roll the dough into a log. Slice into portions.
Boil in salted water for 10 minutes, then transfer to a baking dish.
Pour sour cream over the top. Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden.

name: Stuffed Cabbage Rolls (Holubtsi)
reasons: Technique baked -> simmered; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Core the cabbage. Blanch whole head in boiling water for 3–4 minutes. Peel off softened outer leaves and repeat.
Mix pork mince with par-cooked rice, sautéed onion, salt, and pepper.
Place filling on each leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Make sauce: fry grated carrot and onion, add tomato paste, stock, and sour cream.
Arrange rolls tightly in a pot. Pour sauce over. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 50–60 minutes. Serve with extra sour cream.

name: Sushi Set
reasons: Technique fried -> raw; follow the stored preparation steps. Cold assembled dishes use the existing raw category, which does not imply all ingredients are uncooked.

steps.display_text: Cook short-grain rice, then season with a mixture of rice vinegar, sugar, and salt. Fan to cool.
For nigiri: wet your hands, shape small ovals of rice, press a slice of fish on top with a dab of wasabi.
For maki rolls: lay nori on a bamboo mat, spread rice over it, add filling across the centre.
Roll tightly using the mat, seal the edge with a damp finger, then slice into pieces with a wet knife.
Arrange on a plate with pickled ginger, wasabi, and soy sauce for dipping.

name: Tandoori Chicken
reasons: Technique pan_fry -> baked; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Make deep cuts in chicken legs. Mix yogurt, lemon juice, tandoori masala, garlic paste, and ginger paste.
Coat chicken generously in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (overnight is best).
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a tray.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until edges are slightly charred.
Brush with melted butter in the last 5 minutes for extra flavour.
Serve with sliced onion, lemon wedges, and mint chutney.

name: Tarator (Balkan Cold Yogurt Soup)
reasons: Technique simmered -> raw; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
No heated cooking; retain 15 min hands-on work and include the required 30 min chill.
Normalize the time tier and quick-meal tag to strict under-30 / under-45 / under-60 boundaries.

steps.display_text: Finely grate cucumber and squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix yogurt with cold water to a soup-like consistency.
Add cucumber, crushed garlic, chopped walnuts, and fresh dill.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes. Serve in chilled bowls with ice cubes if desired.

name: Tavë Kosi (Albanian Baked Lamb)
reasons: Technique pan_fry -> baked; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Cut lamb into pieces. Season and brown in butter on all sides until golden.
Add rice and enough water to cover. Parboil together for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a baking dish. Preheat oven to 190°C.
Whisk yogurt with eggs until completely smooth. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Pour custard evenly over the lamb and rice.
Bake for 45 minutes until custard is set and golden on top. Serve straight from the dish.
